notes.title: CTS — Early Access is LIVE! (Launched Sept 25, 13:00 GMT) 🚂📦
notes.notes: [p]Hello Operators![/p][p]Today we’re excited to finally share CTS with you in Early Access. Build and manage your own [b]rail container terminal[/b] — accept trains, operate cranes, organize yard logistics, and grow a small park into a major logistics hub.[/p][p][b]What’s in this Early Access:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Core gameplay loop: train arrivals, unloading, yard stacking and truck pickups.[/p][/*][*][p]Economic system with upgrades, tariffs and maintenance.[/p][/*][*][p]Day/Night cycle, dynamic soundtrack and detailed stats.[/p][/*][*][p]Full localization: English / Russian / Spanish (voice prompts + UI).[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Launch special:[/b] 10% off for the first 72 hours.[/p][p][b]Known issues & hotfix plan:[/b] we’ve tested carefully, but if you find critical bugs, please post them here or on Discord — we’ll prioritize and push hotfixes fast.[/p][p][b]Where to start:[/b] wishlist if you haven’t yet, check the tutorial, and try the “Quick Start” yard scenario for a guided experience.[/p][p]Thank you for your support — see you at the terminal![/p][p][/p][p]— Tikam[/p]

notes.title: Devlog #2 — Container types & yard management revealed
notes.notes:
[h1]Devlog #2 — Container types & yard logic 🚂📦[/h1][p align="start"]Hello everyone! 👋
Today we’re diving into a key part of CTS — the way different container types are handled and how the yard itself functions. Since our terminal is built around [b]railway logistics[/b], we wanted to design a system that feels both realistic and rewarding to manage.[/p][h3]🚛 Container types[/h3][p align="start"]In CTS, trains deliver containers of different sizes and weights. At this stage, we’re focusing on [b]20ft and 40ft dry containers[/b], which already form the backbone of the yard flow. Each type has its own handling requirements, affecting storage space, crane operations, and the timing of departures.
Later on, we plan to expand the system with [b]specialized container types[/b] (reefer, tank, open-top, etc.), but for now we’re concentrating on making the core gameplay loop solid and polished.[/p][h3]🏗 Yard logic[/h3][p align="start"]The yard is divided into rows and stacks, and every decision you make about where to place a container affects overall efficiency. Right now the logic includes:[/p][list][*][p][b]Weight distribution[/b] — heavier containers need to be placed lower in stacks.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Train compatibility[/b] — certain wagons can only take containers of specific lengths.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Truck pickup flow[/b] — when trucks arrive, containers need to be accessible without excessive reshuffling.[/p][/*][/list][p align="start"]Each of these mechanics ties into the simulation layer, so poor planning can lead to delays, while efficient stacking gives you smoother operations and higher throughput.[/p][h3]🔧 What’s next[/h3][p align="start"]Over the next updates we’ll continue improving yard mechanics, refining stacking rules, and expanding the container pool. Our long-term goal is to make every logistical choice matter, so even a small decision in placement can change the rhythm of the terminal.[/p][p align="start"]That’s all for today’s devlog! Thank you for following along 🚂📦 Your feedback and wishlists mean the world to us — it helps us build CTS into the container terminal simulator we’ve always wanted to play.[/p][p align="start"]See you at the yard! 👷‍♂️[/p]

notes.title: Devlog #1 — Introducing CTS and the road ahead
notes.notes: [p]Hello, Operators, and welcome to the very first development diary for [i]Container Terminal Simulator[/i] (CTS)![/p][p align="start"]In this devlog series we’ll be sharing behind-the-scenes stories, gameplay decisions, technical improvements, and future plans — everything that goes into building the railway terminal of our dreams. Our goal is not just to show progress, but to develop CTS [b]together with the community[/b] from the very start.[/p][h3]What’s happening right now?[/h3][p align="start"]At this stage we’re finishing work on the [b]core gameplay loop[/b]: receiving freight trains full of containers, distributing them across unloading zones, operating gantry cranes and yard trucks, then sending the cargo further by road transport. Every action you take impacts your [b]profit, processing speed, and reputation[/b] among logistics clients.[/p][p align="start"]In parallel we’re working on:[/p][list][*][p]a complete [b]economic system[/b] with tariffs, upgrades, equipment wear, downtime and contracts;[/p][/*][*][p]re-designing the [b]UI[/b] for clarity and immersion;[/p][/*][*][p]adding a day/night cycle and [i]dynamic soundtrack[/i] that reflects the rhythm of a busy rail terminal.[/p][/*][/list][h3]Why devlogs?[/h3][p align="start"]CTS is a project where realism, strategy and atmosphere are equally important. We’d love to involve you in the process — your feedback and wishlist directly influence what gets added, reworked or balanced.[/p][p align="start"]In the next posts we’ll talk about:[/p][list][*][p]container types and cargo behaviour,[/p][/*][*][p]yard planning tools,[/p][/*][*][p]and when you’ll be able to try the [b]public Steam demo[/b].[/p][/*][/list][p align="start"]Thanks for joining us at this early stage — and please [b]add CTS to your wishlist[/b] — that’s the best way to support us right now 💙[/p]

notes.title: Release moved to September
notes.notes:
[p]After careful consideration, we have decided to [b]move our Early Access release to September 2025[/b].
During the final submission process, we identified a critical issue related to localization and save-game behavior. Rather than releasing with such a bug, we’ve chosen to delay the public launch in order to deliver a more stable experience.[/p][p align="start"]✨ Over the next weeks we will:[/p][list][*][p]squash the localization/save bug;[/p][/*][*][p]run a [i]small closed testing round[/i] (keys will be sent to selected testers);[/p][/*][*][p]polish the UI & stability;[/p][/*][*][p]finalize our content roadmap for Early Access updates.[/p][/*][/list][p align="start"]🎯 New target window: [b]mid-late September 2025.[/b][/p][p align="start"]Thank you for your patience, wishlist support, and all the kind words — it really keeps us going.
See you at the terminal soon! 🚢📦[/p]
